title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as NASA considers new headquarters and potential Hubble upgrades, while various partnerships and funding rounds signal a robust private sector. Meanwhile, defense tech continues to attract attention, with a notable focus on space resilience and tactical capabilities.

themes.title: NASA's Headquarters Hunt
themes.body: NASA is on the verge of selecting a new headquarters building, a move that could signal a shift in its operational focus. This decision, expected by year-end, may reflect the agency's evolving priorities in a rapidly changing space landscape.

themes.title: Funding and Partnerships Flourish
themes.body: Leaf Space's collaboration with D-Orbit and EnduroSat highlights the growing trend of connectivity services in the space sector. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C round underscores the increasing appetite for investment in space-related ventures.

themes.title: Defense Tech's Space Resilience Push
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup, which adds $1.4B to the space resilience line, signals a commitment to fortifying U.S. capabilities in the face of emerging threats. This aligns with Anduril and L3Harris's tactical SDA constellation bid, emphasizing the intersection of defense and space.

themes.title: Hubble and ISS Concerns
themes.body: NASA's interest in a Hubble reboost hinges on cost reductions, illustrating the agency's tightrope walk between ambition and budget constraints. Additionally, concerns over Russian repairs have prompted a decision to establish safe havens on the ISS, reflecting ongoing geopolitical tensions.
